name: movie_betaaur_isi_orbit
label: Movie: beta Aurigae's orbit with the three ISI trucks in a 45 m triangle at 650 nm, seven consecutive nights (1.77 orbits): the orbital parallax against Hipparcos and the 2026 CHARA orbit
notes: The 1.03 and 0.96 mas twins null at 158 and 170 m at 650 nm and the pair's fringe period lambda/a is 41 m at quadrature (a = 3.29 mas): the trucks in a 45 m equilateral triangle (projected baselines 23-45 m at three position angles 60 deg apart) sit inside the first lobe (disk |V|^2 0.74) and sweep a full fringe every night, |V|^2 running from ~0 to 0.8. Dec +45: 10.5 h per night above 30 deg at Palomar, twice Spica's window, which repays the factor two in flux.

Seven nights from phase 0.2 cover 1.77 of the 3.96 d orbit. The partial eclipses (i = 76.8, a cos i = 0.75 mas against R1 + R2 = 1.00 mas) last 6 h and cover 13 % of the orbit; 38-52 % of the blocks on four of the seven nights fall within hbtsim's near-eclipse margin, are rendered through the two-disk image grid and are dropped from the separation fit. The fit holds the radii fixed and scales the system, so a is the orbital parallax: with the spectroscopic a (AU) known to a few tenths of a percent, sigma(a)/a is sigma(d)/d.

Expected (Fisher): sigma(a)/a 0.7 %, sigma(node) 0.3 deg after seven nights, one chi^2 island from night 2. Kepler's law with the Southworth et al. 2007 masses gives 3.29 mas at the Hipparcos 24.87 pc; the 2026 CHARA orbit found 3.365 mas at 24.30 pc (2.3 % apart): the week decides between them. A 30 m side gives 0.9 % and 0.5 deg.

Not modelled: the diameters are not free parameters (a two-side schedule, 30 + 60 m, would separate them from the distance) and the eclipse blocks, where |V|^2 encodes the limb-darkened overlap, are not fitted.
